Marker.purpose: Catalogue definition of a single measurable health signal — its LOINC code, canonical unit, within-pillar weight, green/yellow/red clinical band functions, two-sided flag, measurement tier (Core/Peripheral/Comprehensive), decay class, critical-flag, escalation rule, reservoir links, and sex-axis (none | gonadal | natal). Marker is read-only configuration; it owns no patient data. Band functions are parameterised by cohort (age, sex, disease, medication, hormonal milieu) and must be re-verified on each guideline cadence (D19, D20). Weights are defaults, cohort-adjusted at scoring time (Doc 03 §3, Doc 09).

stories.want: look up the band thresholds and within-pillar weight for a given marker resolved to a patient's cohort context
stories.soThat: it can compute the correct clinical risk score r_i without embedding band logic in the aggregator
acceptance: Given marker_id='apob' and cohort={age:45,sex:'M',disease:[],medications:[]}, When the engine calls Marker.band(cohort), Then it returns green:<80, yellow:80-99, red:>=100 (mg/dL) per ESC/EAS and weight=0.18

Given the same marker and cohort={medications:['statin']}, When Marker.band(cohort) is called, Then the returned thresholds are unchanged (band reflects biology, not medication effect — MANAGED state is set separately by ManagedState, D3)
Given marker_id='hdl' with two_sided=true, When Marker.band(cohort={sex:'F'}) is called, Then both low-adverse (<40 mg/dL red) and high-normal (>=50 green) thresholds are returned
Given a guideline bump is proposed via admin-constants, When the model-version gate runs, Then the band function for affected markers is updated only after clinician approval and re-validation (D20)
edge: Sex-hormone markers (estradiol, FSH) with sex_axis='gonadal' must resolve bands from the patient's life-stage and HRT status (Doc 05, D15); a missing life-stage falls back to natal-sex defaults with confidence penalty
A marker band using cohort percentiles (HRV, VO2max) that has no reference distribution for the patient's cohort cell must fall back to the nearest super-cohort and lower confidence (D7)

stories.want: flag a marker as critical and specify its escalation rule
stories.soThat: the scoring engine can apply a hard pillar-cap and route a confirmed red to the crisis pathway without per-marker special-casing in the aggregator
acceptance: Given Marker.critical=true and a confirmed measurement in the red band, When the CriticalCascade runs, Then the pillar score is capped at <=40 and an escalation event is emitted (Doc 03 §6)

Given PHQ-9 item-9 suicidality answer > 0, When the marker's escalation_rule='suicidality_override' fires, Then the MCS pillar is forced to red/critical regardless of total PHQ-9 score (Doc 02 §P12 hard safety rule)
Given Marker.critical=false (e.g. VO2max deficit), When the marker enters red, Then it is classified as a reserve-deficit red (priority-improvement) and does NOT trigger the cascade
edge: A marker straddling acute-danger and reserve-deficit semantics (SpO2) must be classified as critical=true; the data-quality layer may lower confidence to reconfirm-pending before cascade (D14)
Changing critical=true to false requires a model-version bump and governance sign-off (D20, admin-constants)

stories.want: validate that an incoming value is within the physiological plausibility range defined on the Marker
stories.soThat: out-of-range values are routed to the QA queue rather than silently corrupting the score
acceptance: Given marker_id='potassium' with plausibility_range=[1.5, 9.0] mmol/L, When a value of 12.0 is ingested, Then the measurement is rejected with 422 implausible and enqueued for QA review
Given marker_id='hba1c' and value=5.2 (within range), When ingested with source='lab' and trust_tier='lab_venous', Then the measurement is persisted with q_source=1.0 and no QA flag
edge: A value within plausible range but extreme relative to the patient's personal baseline (z > 4) must be flagged 'reconfirm pending' per D14, not rejected outright — it may be a genuine acute event
A plausibility range for derived markers (HOMA-IR, FIB-4) depends on the constituent inputs being present; missing inputs must yield 422 with a structured error naming the missing components

table.name: marker_def

columns.name: marker_id
columns.note: stable slug e.g. 'apob', 'hba1c'

columns.name: loinc_code
columns.note: canonical LOINC; NULL for derived/survey markers

columns.name: unit
columns.note: canonical unit after ingestion normalisation

columns.name: pillar_id
columns.note: one home pillar

columns.name: tier
columns.note: C | P | X (Core/Peripheral/Comprehensive)

columns.name: two_sided
columns.note: true if both low and high are adverse

columns.name: sex_axis
columns.note: none | gonadal | natal (D15)

columns.name: weight_default
columns.note: within-pillar weight w_i (cohort-adjusted at scoring time)

columns.name: decay_class
columns.note: short | medium | permanent (τ_i half-life)

columns.name: critical
columns.note: true => CriticalCascade on confirmed red

columns.name: escalation_rule
columns.note: structured escalation spec (threshold, pathway, override condition)

columns.name: plausibility_range
columns.note: QA gate; outside => 422 + QA queue

columns.name: skew_transform
columns.note: true => log-scale personal baseline z (D13)

columns.name: reservoir_links
columns.note: reservoir_ids this marker feeds

columns.name: band_fn_ref
columns.note: evidence IDs for green/yellow/red thresholds (D19)

columns.name: model_version
columns.note: version that last changed this row

table.notes: Rows are versioned via model_version; no in-place edits to band thresholds — a change creates a new model_version row and requires governance sign-off (D20, admin-constants). Band logic is not stored as raw numbers but as parameterised function references (band_fn_ref → evidence_registry) to allow cohort-contextual resolution at query time.

invariants: Every Marker must reference at least one valid evidence_registry entry for its band thresholds (D19); a Marker without a band_fn_ref cannot be activated in production
critical=true markers must have a non-null escalation_rule; activating a critical Marker with a null rule is a deploy-time constraint violation
weight_default values within a pillar must sum to approximately 1.0 (±0.01 tolerance); deviations must be flagged at model-version validation time (D17)
Changing any band threshold or weight_default requires a model-version bump, clinician approval, and re-running the validation harness before the new values are live (D20)

A Marker with sex_axis='gonadal' must define band overrides for each applicable life-stage in the band_fn_ref table; missing overrides fall back to natal-sex defaults, not silently to a universal range (D15)
plausibility_range must be strictly wider than the red band extremes; values inside the red band but outside plausibility_range are a configuration error flagged at load time

Measurement.purpose: Immutable time-series record of a single observed value for one patient and one marker at a given effectiveTime. Every reading persists as its own row — the score is always re-derivable from the history. Each Measurement carries: source (lab | wearable | survey | derived | literature_fallback), trust_tier (lab_venous | clinical_grade_device | consumer_validated | inferential | survey), raw q_source (from the trust-tier table, D22), and a computed confidence_i(t) that decays with staleness (Doc 01 §2). Partitioned by (patient_id, effectiveTime) for time-series query patterns. Idempotency is enforced via an idempotency_key (source system + message id); duplicate ingestion returns 409 without creating a second row.

stories.want: persist a new wearable SpO2 reading with its trust tier and derive q_source automatically
stories.soThat: the scoring engine always has a correct, trust-aware confidence value without manual intervention
acceptance: Given source='wearable', device_grade='consumer_validated', value=95.0, When the measurement is persisted, Then trust_tier='consumer_validated', q_source=0.7 (midpoint of 0.6–0.8 range per Doc 01 §2, D22), and confidence_i(t=now)=0.7

Given source='wearable', device_grade='inferential', value=72 (readiness score), When persisted, Then trust_tier='inferential', q_source is set to informational-only sentinel (e.g. 0.0 effective band weight), and the measurement cannot contribute to a band classification
Given source='lab', device_grade=null, When persisted, Then trust_tier='lab_venous', q_source=1.0
Given the same patient + marker + effectiveTime + idempotency_key already exists, When re-ingested, Then the API returns 409 and no second row is created
edge: A wearable SpO2 reading of 88% with trust_tier='consumer_validated' must be stored but must NOT trigger the critical cascade without a clinical-grade confirmation — it may only raise Watch/Advisory (D22, wearable-critical-gate)

A measurement with source='literature_fallback' must never be written by the ingestion worker; it is synthesised by the scoring engine when no real measurement exists and the patient's cohort median is used as a neutral prior (Doc 01 §4.3)

stories.want: retrieve the latest effective confidence-weighted value for each marker at scoring time, with recency decay applied
stories.soThat: stale measurements are automatically down-weighted and replaced by the literature fallback once they drop below the stale floor
acceptance: Given a Measurement with effectiveTime=90 days ago and decay_class='medium' (τ≈60 days), When confidence_i(t) is computed, Then confidence_i = q_source * exp(-90/60) ≈ 0.22 for a lab measurement (q_source=1.0)

Given confidence_i < per-marker stale_floor, When the scoring engine resolves the marker value, Then source is set to literature_fallback, confidence is set to the literature_fallback q_source (0.2–0.4), and the pillar's coverage metric is decremented
Given a permanent-decay marker (Lp(a), genetics, τ=∞), When confidence_i is computed regardless of age, Then it never decays below q_source (exp(-t/∞) = 1)
edge: A CGM-derived time-in-range value (source='derived', tier='comprehensive') must carry the minimum q_source of its constituent raw CGM readings — if any constituent is consumer_validated, the derived value cannot exceed q_source=0.8

When multiple Measurements exist for the same patient + marker within the same day (e.g., two BP readings), the scoring engine must use the most recent by effectiveTime unless the older reading has significantly higher trust_tier, in which case the implementation-defined blending rule from Doc 03 §3 applies

stories.want: reconstruct the exact PureScore at any historical point-in-time using only the Measurement time-series
stories.soThat: the system is fully auditable and a score can never be improved by deleting an unfavourable measurement
acceptance: Given all Measurement rows for a patient up to timestamp T, When the scoring engine is replayed at T, Then it produces the same PureScore that was emitted live at T (deterministic replay invariant)

Given a patient deletes a red Measurement record (or it is soft-deleted), When the score is recomputed, Then coverage drops and the pillar score is not improved — the reservoir layer retains the burden accumulated by that measurement (Doc 01 §5 anti-gaming, Doc 04)
edge: A measurement marked with data_quality_flag='artifact' (D14) is retained in the time-series with confidence forced to ~0; it is not deleted, and the QA audit trail records the flag reason

GDPR right-to-erasure requests must be handled by anonymisation, not deletion, to preserve time-series integrity for clinical audit — a legal hold flag prevents physical deletion until the retention period expires (Doc 11)

stories.want: query the time-series for a marker to build a personal baseline distribution for early-warning z-score computation
stories.soThat: the z-score reflects genuine personal drift rather than population noise
acceptance: Given >=N_min (per-marker) Measurements with confidence above a threshold, When the PersonalBaseline is built, Then mean and std are computed on the log-transformed series for skew-tagged markers (D13) and on the raw series for others

Given <N_min Measurements, When PersonalBaseline is requested, Then the empirical-Bayes prior (cohort mean and std) is used with full shrinkage weight (D6), and the EarlyWarning layer operates on the population baseline only until sufficient personal data accrues

Given a Measurement is ingested that is z>3 from the personal baseline, When confidence is full (not artifact-flagged), When the marker is critical=true, Then a confirmed critical cascade is triggered (not merely Watch)
edge: If a patient changes their wearable device mid-stream (different calibration), the PersonalBaseline must restart from the device-change date or apply a calibration offset if one is available — the personal mean/std across device generations is not directly comparable
Seasonal variation in markers (e.g. vitamin D, mood PRO scores) must not be mistaken for a trend — the baseline engine should account for annual cyclicity where flagged on the Marker definition

table.name: measurement

columns.name: patient_id
columns.note: partition key

columns.name: effective_time
columns.note: partition sort key; when the measurement was taken, not when it was ingested

columns.name: ingested_at
columns.note: server wall-clock ingestion timestamp

columns.name: value
columns.note: in canonical unit from marker_def; NULL for categorical markers stored in value_text

columns.name: value_text
columns.note: for categorical / PRO answers

columns.name: source
columns.note: lab | wearable | survey | derived | literature_fallback

columns.name: trust_tier
columns.note: lab_venous | clinical_grade_device | consumer_validated | inferential | survey | literature_fallback

columns.name: q_source
columns.note: base source quality [0,1]; informational-only=0 sentinel for inferential

columns.name: device_id
columns.note: for wearable readings; enables device-change baseline reset

columns.name: idempotency_key
columns.note: source-system message-id to prevent duplicate ingest

columns.name: data_quality_flag
columns.note: null | artifact | reconfirm_pending (D14)

columns.name: confidence_at_ingest
columns.note: q_source (decay=1 at effective_time); decayed value computed at query time

columns.name: provenance
columns.note: lab order ref, wearable reading id, survey response id, or fallback cohort citation

columns.name: model_version
columns.note: version active at ingest time (for replay)

indexes: PARTITION BY RANGE (effective_time) — monthly or quarterly partitions
INDEX (patient_id, marker_id, effective_time DESC) — primary time-series access pattern
INDEX (patient_id, data_quality_flag) WHERE data_quality_flag IS NOT NULL — QA queue
INDEX (patient_id, trust_tier, effective_time DESC) — trust-tier filtered queries
table.notes: Append-only by design — no UPDATE or DELETE in the hot path. Soft-deletion via data_quality_flag='deleted' with audit trail. GDPR erasure = anonymisation + legal hold flag, not physical row deletion. literature_fallback rows are written by the ScoringEngine, not the IngestionWorker, and carry provenance pointing to the ReferenceDist row used.

invariants: Rows are immutable once written; corrections are new rows with a supersedes_id foreign key pointing to the corrected row, and the old row retains data_quality_flag='superseded'
A measurement with trust_tier='inferential' must have q_source=0 (informational sentinel) and must never produce a band classification or trigger a critical cascade (D22)
A wearable-only anomaly (no clinical-grade corroboration) for a critical marker must produce at most a Watch/Advisory early-warning event — it cannot fire the CriticalCascade (D22)
Idempotency_key uniqueness per (patient_id, marker_id) is a hard constraint; a duplicate ingest returns 409 without side-effects
confidence_i(t) is always derived dynamically at query time from q_source and (t − effective_time) / τ_i — it is never stored as a static column to avoid staleness of the stored value

A measurement cannot improve the PureScore or clear a reservoir burden by being deleted or flagged artifact — the reservoir system retains burden from confirmed historical measurements (Doc 01 §5, Doc 04)

InputStream.purpose: Logical envelope for one of the four flagged input domains — LAB (🧪), WEAR (⌚), GOAL (🎯), LIFE (📝) — as defined in Doc 01 §1 and Doc 18 §1. InputStream is not a row-level entity; it is the classification layer that tags every inbound payload before it becomes a Measurement. It resolves the trust tier and q_source floor for the stream, routes to the appropriate ingestion worker, and carries the per-stream confidence ceiling that the scoring engine applies when a patient's data comes predominantly from one stream. For WEAR, InputStream enforces D22 wearable trust tiering: clinical-grade sub-stream (CGM, validated cuff, single-lead ECG) vs consumer-validated vs inferential-only. For LIFE, it applies the survey trust floor (q_source 0.5–0.7). GOAL feeds the weighting/personalisation layer, not measurements directly.

stories.want: classify an inbound wearable payload by its device class and assign the correct D22 trust tier before creating Measurement rows
stories.soThat: the downstream scoring engine never needs to re-derive trust from device metadata — it is stamped once at ingestion
acceptance: Given a wearable payload with device_class='clinical_grade_device' (e.g. validated continuous BP cuff), When InputStream.classify() runs, Then all Measurement rows carry trust_tier='clinical_grade_device' and q_source in [0.85, 1.0]
Given a wearable payload with device_class='consumer_validated' (e.g. consumer smartwatch resting HR), When classified, Then trust_tier='consumer_validated' and q_source in [0.6, 0.8]

Given a wearable payload with device_class='inferential' (e.g. HRV-derived readiness score), When classified, Then trust_tier='inferential', q_source=0 (informational sentinel), and no Measurement row for this payload may contribute to a band classification or headline score
Given a lab HL7/FHIR payload from an accredited lab (stream='LAB'), When classified, Then trust_tier='lab_venous' and q_source=1.0 regardless of wearable device rules
edge: A device in the device registry that has lost its validation certification (e.g. removed from the validated-device list) must be downgraded from consumer_validated to inferential at the InputStream layer, retroactively flagging all future Measurements from that device — historical Measurements are not retroactively changed but a note is added to the device record

A mixed payload from a hub that aggregates both clinical-grade CGM and inferential stress scores must split into two InputStream sub-streams and stamp each Measurement row with its own trust_tier — the higher-trust device class must not bleed into the inferential metrics

stories.want: know the q_source confidence ceiling for each stream contributing to a patient's current data mix
stories.soThat: it can accurately compute the companion Confidence dimension and suppress over-confident green claims when data is predominantly from low-trust streams
acceptance: Given a patient whose marker coverage is 80% WEAR (consumer_validated) and 20% LAB, When the Confidence companion dimension is computed, Then it reflects the blended q_source ceiling and is labelled 'moderate confidence — limited lab data'

Given a patient with no LAB data and all markers from LIFE (survey, q_source 0.5–0.7), When a pillar score is 'green', Then it must be labelled 'low-coverage green' and the pillar coverage metric is visibly low (Doc 01 §4.3)

Given a GOAL stream update (user sets a new weight-loss goal), When processed, Then it does NOT create a Measurement row — it updates the patient's Goal record and re-ranks nudges; q_source is not applicable to GOAL stream events
edge: A patient who provides only LIFE (self-reported lifestyle PRO) data and no LAB or WEAR data cannot receive a red/critical classification solely from self-report (survey q_source 0.5–0.7 is insufficient to confirm a critical without clinical corroboration) — the system must issue a 'measure this' nudge and hold the marker at Watch, not cascade

If the WEAR stream is temporarily unavailable (device offline, consent withdrawn), the affected markers must fall back to their last confirmed Measurement with decayed confidence, not to a literature fallback that could mask a genuine adverse trend already in the personal baseline

stories.want: verify that each InputStream type has the correct consent scope active before data is ingested
stories.soThat: PHI from genetic, reproductive, or wearable streams is never processed without the patient's active consent for that scope
acceptance: Given a LAB payload containing ApoE genotype (genetic data), When ingested, When the patient lacks an active 'genetic_data' consent scope, Then the payload is rejected with 401 and a consent-required error — not silently dropped
Given a WEAR payload from a continuous CGM (clinical-grade), When the patient has active consent for 'wearable_clinical' scope, Then ingestion proceeds normally

Given a consent withdrawal POST /v1/patients/{id}/consent removing the 'wearable' scope, When a subsequent WEAR payload arrives, Then InputStream rejects the payload with 401 and existing Measurement rows from that stream are flagged for retention-policy review
edge: Ramadan fasting context (D21) alters the clinical interpretation of glucose readings from the CGM sub-stream — the InputStream must pass a context_flags field alongside the Measurement to allow the scoring engine to apply the IDF-DAR safety rule without modifying the raw value

A LIFE stream response that triggers a validated PRO (e.g., PHQ-9 score computed from individual item responses) must have the PRO composite written as a derived Measurement with source='derived' and trust_tier inheriting the survey floor, not a new InputStream classification

table.name: input_stream_event

columns.name: event_id
columns.note: correlates all Measurement rows produced by one inbound payload

columns.name: stream_type
columns.note: LAB | WEAR | GOAL | LIFE

columns.name: device_class
columns.note: clinical_grade_device | consumer_validated | inferential | null (for LAB/LIFE/GOAL)

columns.name: trust_tier_resolved
columns.note: trust tier stamped onto all Measurement rows from this event (D22)

columns.name: q_source_ceiling
columns.note: maximum q_source for any Measurement from this event; 0 for inferential

columns.name: received_at
columns.note: server ingestion wall-clock

columns.name: source_system_id
columns.note: lab LIS id, wearable platform id, app session id

columns.name: idempotency_key
columns.note: prevents duplicate payload processing

columns.name: consent_scopes_verified
columns.note: scopes checked at ingest time; rejection logged if missing

columns.name: context_flags
columns.note: e.g. {ramadan: true, hrt_active: true} passed to scoring engine alongside Measurement rows

columns.name: measurement_count
columns.note: number of Measurement rows produced by this event

columns.name: status
columns.note: accepted | rejected | partial (some rows QA-held)

indexes: INDEX (patient_id, received_at DESC) — recent events per patient
UNIQUE (patient_id, idempotency_key) — idempotency at event level
INDEX (patient_id, stream_type, received_at DESC) — stream-type filtered queries
INDEX (status) WHERE status != 'accepted' — QA / error monitoring
table.notes: input_stream_event is an envelope/audit record; the Measurement table is the data of record. GOAL stream events do not produce Measurement rows — they produce Goal updates and are recorded here for consent audit only. Rejected events are retained with status='rejected' and rejection_reason for compliance audit. The trust_tier_resolved and q_source_ceiling columns are the single source of truth for stream trust — they must never be overridden downstream without a new event record.

invariants: Every Measurement row must trace back to exactly one input_stream_event (via event_id); orphan Measurements are a data-integrity violation

A WEAR stream event with device_class='inferential' must produce Measurement rows with trust_tier='inferential' and q_source=0; no downstream pathway may reclassify these to a higher trust tier without a new corroborating event of clinical_grade_device or lab_venous tier (D22)
A stream event must be rejected at the consent-scope check before any Measurement rows are written; partial writes after a consent failure are a transaction integrity violation
Idempotency is enforced at the event level (input_stream_event) and at the Measurement level independently — both uniqueness constraints must be enforced to prevent partial duplicate processing
A GOAL stream event must never set trust_tier or q_source on any Measurement row — GOAL data feeds the Goal entity and personalisation layer exclusively, not the Measurement time-series
q_source_ceiling on an event must equal the minimum q_source of all constituent device classes in the payload — a mixed payload cannot inherit the highest trust tier present
